claims.text: A controlled, optimized thermal treatment will reduce post-exposure toughness degradation in the high-entropy alloy.
The thermal treatment will stabilize the alloy's grain structure.
The thermal treatment will stabilize grain boundaries.
The thermal treatment will prevent deleterious phase transformations.
Grain-boundary stabilization and prevention of deleterious phase transformations will reduce toughness degradation.
The proposed treatment or exposure operates within 500–800 °C for 1–10 hours under minimal or no external stress.
The treated alloy will retain its original strength–ductility combination after service-relevant heating.
The treated alloy will exhibit less toughness degradation than an untreated alloy having identical composition and processing history.
Charpy impact testing, microscopy, and tensile testing can measure the proposed toughness, microstructural, and strength–ductility responses.
Significantly lower toughness in the treated alloy than in the untreated baseline would falsify the hypothesis.
Any altered microstructure in the treated alloy relative to the untreated baseline would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis expects treatment-induced stabilization or preservation of grain and phase structure, which may produce a microstructural difference from the untreated post-exposure baseline, but the falsification rule treats any altered microstructure as falsifying. The rule should instead specify an adverse change or failure to achieve the predicted stabilization.
